title: Rain-wet bare soil: show it or keep hiding it?
question: When rain falls on bare tilled soil (nothing planted), the soil really is watered — plant there and the seed starts life already wet, which is true and useful. But showing that wetness once confused a playtester ('I can water tiles without a plant?'), so it's currently hidden: wet ground only draws where something is growing. Hiding it fixed the confusion and lost a true signal. This is the last open sliver of a bigger fix that already shipped.
why_now: Small, but it's been open for days and it gates nothing — a thirty-second call. Also worth knowing: the watering can's own 'state shows before the tap' treatment (a droplet on watered crops) shipped, so the vocabulary for showing wetness now exists.

options.label: Keep it hidden
options.detail: Status quo. Bare soil never draws wet; the plant-here-now signal stays invisible.

options.label: Show it
options.detail: Wet bare soil draws wet. True, useful, and possibly confusing again — could be revisited after the next fresh-adult session.

options.label: Show it differently
options.detail: E.g. only a subtle droplet mark rather than the full wet-soil tint. Write the idea in the judgment box.
